record.title: Mingbird reports improved artifact completion by small local models on a bounded agent benchmark
record.summary: The authors compare a local-first agent harness with three stock harnesses across four small open models and 18 self-built tasks, reporting an average task score of 0.886 for Mingbird versus 0.631, 0.479 and 0.405 for the named baselines. A separate 278-task tau-squared comparison reports 0.856 under a common user simulator. The paper publishes per-cell results and discusses artifact checks, finish gates and anti-loop controls. These are author-reported benchmark results: the primary matrix uses one machine, one counted run per cell and tasks co-developed with some harness mechanisms.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the paper’s 18-task primary benchmark, the authors report an average score of 0.886 for Mingbird versus 0.631, 0.479 and 0.405 for three named stock harnesses across four tested small models.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports a score of 0.856 on a separate 278-task tau-squared comparison using a common user simulator.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper’s mechanism counts include 40 finish-gate refusals for missing named artifacts and 34 loop interceptions across 288 published cells; the authors caution that mechanism incidence is not causal attribution.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent multi-run replication on independently authored tasks.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains transfer beyond the authors’ benchmark, finish checks and feedback handling could improve the task completion of small open models on local systems. The main result is in-sample and single-run, so the consequence is substantial only if independently replicated.
limitations: Primary benchmark is self-built with one machine and one counted run per cell; task families are correlated.
Some mechanisms were developed with the primary task set in the loop, so ablation estimates are in-sample and directional.
The external tau-squared comparison has protocol deviations described by the authors and is not a fully independent replication.
Scores do not establish broad general intelligence, user-valued work quality or production reliability.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report higher benchmark scores than named stock harnesses and describe artifact checks as a way to prevent premature completion.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and its public per-cell artifact are accessible; the research desk did not reproduce the task outcomes.
technical.mechanism: Local-first harness adds artifact-aware finish gating, anti-loop monitoring and verification feedback to small open-model agents.
technical.regime: Four small open models on 18 self-built primary tasks, plus 278 tasks in a separate benchmark comparison; single machine and one counted run per cell.
technical.strongest_baseline: Three named stock harnesses and a separate common-simulator tau-squared comparison.

brief.title: Mingbird reports improved artifact completion by small local models on a bounded agent benchmark
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced on independently designed tasks, artifact-aware stopping and feedback controls could make small local models more useful for practical agent work. The available comparisons do not show broad capability transfer or isolate the effect of individual harness mechanisms.
